coverage:
Read in full: src/core/editing/{history,commands,snapshot-history,canvas-history,sprite-history,classic-domain-history,document-history,bound-edit-history,undo-stack,save-coordinator,section-ops}.ts; src/renderer/state/{editorStore,classicLevelStore,canvasStore,artStore,projectStore,history-factories,history-hub,aeon-save,import-sheet}.ts; spriteStore.ts:250-620; src/renderer/hooks/useHistoryVersion.ts; shell/{dirty-tabs,dirty-snapshot,tab-activation/dispatch,tab-activation/level}.ts; components/classic/{composer-shared,classic-surface}.ts(x) plus the commit paths of TileTab/ChunkTab; providers/palette-aeon.ts:100-340; MapViewport.tsx paint/drag/stamp regions (744-790, 800-1060, 1180-1400, 1500-1545); ComposerCanvas.tsx:180-430; CanvasHost/CanvasMode commit paths; art-facet.tsx:90-200; TilesetPanel.tsx:240-330.

NOT covered by this seat:
- I did not RUN anything — no vitest run, no CDP session. Every finding is static trace; A2/A3/A5 in particular assert runtime event ordering (mouseleave vs mouseup, React synthetic dispatch) that I read but did not observe. A2's \"no window mouseup listener\" rests on a grep of MapViewport.tsx only; if a parent (LevelWorkspace/App/EditorShell) installs a global pointerup that reaches the drag state, A2's severity drops — I did not check the ancestors.
- I did not read the existing history tests to judge whether they assert anything (history-routing.test.ts, aeon-doc-history.test.ts, classicLevelStore.test.ts, canvasStore.test.ts, spriteStore-multidoc.test.ts, document-history.test.ts, bound-edit-history.test.ts, classic-domain-history.test.ts, canvas-history.test.ts). The brief's dominant-defect-class check (\"can you state the input that makes this guard fail?\") was therefore applied to production guards only, NOT to the test suite. That is the single largest gap here — a whole seat's worth of \"do these tests assert nothing?\" is unexamined.
- Untraced command-issuing surfaces: CollisionPalette.tsx, SectionGridNav.tsx, properties-aeon.ts, object-inspector-aeon/classic.ts, PaletteEditor.tsx, map-clipboard.ts / map-stamp.ts (I read the batch-building call sites in MapViewport but not the builders themselves), BlockTab.tsx's assign path, ClassicPalettePanel.tsx, chunk-library-import.ts.
- classic-save.ts / canvas-save.ts / canvas-file.ts save-vs-history interaction (the documented \"dirty is not a doc≠disk oracle after save+undo\" limitation at classicLevelStore.ts:267-279) was read but not audited for a concrete loss scenario.
- Undo interaction with session restore (shell/session-lifecycle.ts restore path, restored canvas/sprite tabs whose stacks are created before their documents load) — only skimmed.

verified_clean: Per-document stack routing is sound and single-sourced: `focusedDocId()` (state/editorStore.ts:205-224) is the ONE resolution used by both `focusedHistory()` (editorStore.ts:234-237) and `executeCommand` (editorStore.ts:388-397), and `ZONE_ART_FACETS` (editorStore.ts:195) is the sole facet→document statement — components/classic/classic-surface.ts:88-92 correctly stopped restating it. Every UI Ctrl+Z binding (workspace/LevelWorkspace.tsx:100-105, components/sprite/SpriteMode.tsx:100-105, components/canvas/CanvasMode.tsx:92-97) drives that same function; none keeps a private stack.

No cross-engine stack bleed. The hub is a singleton (state/history-hub.ts:7) but `registerHistoryFactories` dispatches on `classicIsOpen()` at CONSTRUCTION time (state/history-factories.ts:31-33, 53-65), a project switch calls `resetProjectRuntime()` → `documentHistoryHub.clearAll()` (state/project-runtime.ts:223-226, invoked from shell/session-lifecycle.ts:144), and the same-directory aeon reopen — where the projectKey never changes and the lifecycle reset never fires — has its own explicit `clearAll()` at state/aeon-open.ts:35. A stack built for the wrong engine is caught loudly, not silently: `requireClassicHistory` (state/classicLevelStore.ts:607-620) instanceof-checks and names the offending document.

SnapshotHistory's memory invariant actually holds. `record` pushes then caps (`if (this.undoStack.length > this.maxDepth) this.undoStack.shift()`) and clears redo; `undo`/`redo` each move exactly one entry across (core/editing/snapshot-history.ts:43-64), so `undo.length + redo.length <= maxDepth` at all times — residency is ~N snapshots, not ~2N, exactly as the comment at snapshot-history.ts:19-26 claims. `EditHistory` (core/editing/history.ts:23) caps the same way. No unbounded per-stroke snapshot path exists: ClassicArtSnapshot holds the mutated arrays by REFERENCE (core/editing/classic-domain-history.ts:91-104) and the commands build new arrays copy-on-write (classicLevelStore.ts:867/905/1029), so the only per-entry copy is one `tiles` Uint8Array (tens of KB) — ~8 MB at the 200 default, not a leak.

One-gesture-one-entry holds on every CLASSIC editing path I traced. Tile pixels: TileTab.tsx:248-270 funnels stroke, paste and transform through a single `commitTileBytes` → one `classicEditTiles`. Chunk assign: ChunkTab.tsx:365-403 accumulates the drag in `strokeRef` and emits one `classicEditChunkCells` on an idempotent window-level `endStroke` (composer-shared.tsx:145-153). Paint mode: ChunkTab.tsx:229-261 / BlockTab.tsx:195-215 do diffWrites → planSurfaceEdit → one `classicPaintSurface`, which lands tiles+blocks+colind+chunks in ONE `commitArt` (classicLevelStore.ts:888-991). Layout stamp, object move and start move each commit once on mouseup (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:862-908). commit-canvas is one `classicCommitCanvas` → one `commitArt` across all five art domains (classicLevelStore.ts:1009-1105, invoked once from components/canvas/CommitPlanView.tsx:90).

The classic dirty/undo domain split is enforced, not merely documented. `assertSingleDomain` (classicLevelStore.ts:582-596) throws when a commit names a domain belonging to the other document, and every command's `dirtyPatch` is built from what actually changed (classicLevelStore.ts:968-977, 1096-1101). `pickDomainDirty`/`restoreDomainDirty` (classic-domain-history.ts:30-56) both SET and CLEAR within their own domains, so undoing to a pristine state does not leave a permanent dirty flag and does not clobber the sibling document's flags.

The aeon zone-palette live preview — the original member of the mutate-the-doc-without-history class — is now correctly drained. `previewZone` mutates `z.palette.lines[line].colors[idx]` in place (providers/palette-aeon.ts:224-231) but `beginZoneDrag` snapshots the pre-drag line against the ZONE OBJECT (palette-aeon.ts:200-214), `endZoneDrag` restores it FIRST in every outcome and only then runs `executeAmbientCommand` (palette-aeon.ts:166-197), and `drain` runs both enders unconditionally on teardown (palette-aeon.ts:296-299). The quantized-word comparison (`paletteLineChanged`, palette-aeon.ts:120-124) stops a slider that never left a CRAM level from recording a step. Classic's palette provider previews nothing at all (providers/palette-classic.ts:17-18, 150).

canvasStore's record-vs-dirty split is complete and each setter is auditable against the list at canvasStore.ts:14-34: setPixels/setPalette/setProfile/setGridOrigin record AND dirty (canvasStore.ts:226-301) — exactly the four fields CanvasSnapshot can restore (core/editing/canvas-history.ts:33-39); setSelection/setSource and all view state do neither. Both no-op guards are real: `samePixels` (canvasStore.ts:354-359) compares bytes, and setGridOrigin compares both coordinates before recording (canvasStore.ts:297-298). `openCanvasDoc`/`loadCanvasDoc` explicitly `canvasHistory(docId).clear()` so a reopened id cannot inherit a previous incarnation's stack (canvasStore.ts:438, 460) — the hazard spriteStore avoids differently, via dispose-on-close.

Tab close disposes the right stacks and no more: a level tab drops its own layout stack but keeps `zoneart:<zone>` alive while any other act tab of that zone survives (shell/tab-activation/dispatch.ts:106-120), sprite and canvas closes dispose with their documents (spriteStore.ts:346, canvasStore.ts:524-529), and closing a dirty sprite/canvas tab is confirmed first (dispatch.ts:151-155). The UI act-switch door has a real three-button unsaved-changes confirm whose 'save' branch refuses to fall through to `openAct` on a failed save (shell/tab-activation/level.ts:36-38, 175-197).

Redo invalidation is correct everywhere: `SnapshotHistory.record` sets `this.redoStack = []` (snapshot-history.ts:46) and `EditHistory.execute` sets `this.redoStack = []` (history.ts:24). With per-document stacks there is no sibling-invalidation left to get wrong, which is what retired the old undo-bus (classic-domain-history.ts:12-13). Section-structure ops are pure and non-destructive over history: `removeSection` nulls the slot while the `set-sections` command's `oldSections` still holds the removed Section by reference (core/editing/section-ops.ts:84-96 + history.ts:210-215), so undoing a remove restores the real data rather than a blank.

`ensureCollisionPlanes` (core/collision/collision-cell-resolve.ts:59-63), called outside command dispatch from MapViewport.tsx:786/862/1038 and agent-handler.ts:333/405, seeds the edit planes from `engineCollision` — content-identical to what `resolvePlaneWords(null, engine)` already resolves for a null plane, so a fully-undone gesture leaves the planes allocated but semantically unchanged. Not a correctness defect.

findings.title: MCP `classic-get-level` (a read tool) silently discards the loaded act's unsaved edits and both undo stacks
findings.claim: `classic-get-level` calls `useClassicLevelStore.openAct(ref)` with no dirty check and no confirm; `openAct` disposes both undo stacks and re-reads the LevelDoc from disk with `dirty: {}`, so every unsaved classic edit in the currently-loaded act is destroyed by what the agent surface presents as a read.
findings.evidence: agent-handler.ts:625 `await useClassicLevelStore.getState().openAct(ref);` is reached from the `classic-get-level` case with no guard — the only dirty guard in the whole handler is agent-handler.ts:579, in `classic-open-project`. classicLevelStore.ts:356-357 `disposeStacksFor(get().ref); disposeStacksFor(ref);` drops `level:<zone>:<act>` and `zoneart:<zone>` (classicLevelStore.ts:331-335), classicLevelStore.ts:359 sets `dirty: {}`, and classicLevelStore.ts:401 `const doc = await handle.levels.read(ref)` replaces the doc. There is no same-ref early return, so this fires even when `req.zone/req.act` IS the loaded act. The UI door for the same call has a three-button confirm (shell/tab-activation/level.ts:175-197, planLevelActivation's `classic-confirm` at level.ts:59) — the agent door has none. Failure scenario: user paints 20 minutes of GHZ tile art (dirty.tiles=true), asks the agent "what's in GHZ act 2?", the agent calls classic-get-level → the art is gone from memory, never written to disk, and the undo stack that could recover it is disposed.
findings.fix: Route the agent through the same gate as the tab strip: either call `activateLevelTarget(classicLevelTab(ref).id)` / reuse `planLevelActivation`, or refuse with an error when `Object.values(useClassicLevelStore.getState().dirty).some(Boolean)` and the target ref differs; add a same-ref early return in `openAct` so re-opening the loaded act is a no-op.

verdict.reasoning: Could not refute; traced independently and confirmed. (1) agent-handler.ts:621-625 `classic-get-level` calls `useClassicLevelStore.getState().openAct(ref)` with no dirty check — grepping `dirty`/`planProjectOpen` across the whole 739-line handler yields one hit, line 579 in `classic-open-project`, whose comment states the very policy this case breaks. (2) classicLevelStore.ts:350-362 `openAct` unconditionally runs `disposeStacksFor(get().ref); disposeStacksFor(ref);` (disposing `level:<zone>:<act>` and `zoneart:<zone>`, lines 331-335) and sets `dirty: {}`; there is no same-ref early return in the function — the only same-ref short-circuit lives in the UI planner, shell/tab-activation/level.ts:58, unreachable from the agent path. (3) The doc really is re-read from disk: classicLevelStore.ts:401 `handle.levels.read(ref)` → core/project/s1/index.ts:365-392, which calls `readS1Level(...)` on every invocation; the `readStates` map (line 356) caches only write-side bookkeeping, never the edited doc. No autosave exists anywhere in src (grep autosave|autoSave → nothing), so the lost edits were never persisted. (4) The equivalent UI door has a three-button confirm (level.ts:175-197) plus a save-failure guard (isSaveSuccess, line 37) that exists specifically to stop the fallthrough into openAct. Empirically, an existing repo test already encodes the destructive same-ref semantics and passes at this SHA: classicLevelStore.test.ts:681 edits via classicSetStart/classicSetPalette, calls `openAct(REF)` with the already-loaded REF, and asserts both undo stacks are cleared (`npx vitest run -t "loading a new act clears both"` → 1 passed). Concrete trigger: classic project open on ghz/1, user or agent makes any edit (dirty set, stacks populated), agent calls MCP get_classic_level for any zone/act including ghz/1 itself → edits and both undo stacks destroyed, no prompt, no recovery; the reply then reports the pristine on-disk data as if the edit never happened. Only correction to the finding's framing (not affecting the defect): the MCP description at main/editor-methods.ts:117 does say "Open and read one act", so the surface is not advertised as a pure read — but the name is `get_classic_level`, nothing warns about discarding, and no gate exists, so the loss is still silent.
verdict.severity_correction: Severity stands at critical. It meets the bar literally — silent, unrecoverable loss of unsaved user work (the undo stacks that could restore it are disposed in the same call) — and the codebase's own sibling tool fails closed on this exact hazard. The only argument for downgrading to high is that the trigger requires an agent-driven session, but that is the intended first-class door for this surface, and the self-inflicted variant (edit → get_classic_level to verify → edits erased and pristine data reported back) makes it a routine flow rather than an exotic one.

findings.title: Leaving the aeon map viewport mid-drag drops an object/ring move: doc already mutated, no command, no dirty flag
findings.claim: An object/ring drag mutates `obj.x/obj.y` in place on every mousemove and only becomes a `move-object` command on mouseup; `onMouseLeave` nulls `dragTarget` without committing, so a drag that exits the viewport leaves the placement moved in the document with no undo entry and with `editorStore.dirty` still false — the move is invisible to save and to the unsaved-changes guard.
findings.evidence: MapViewport.tsx:1240-1252 mutates `obj.x = Math.round(...)` / `ring.x = ...` directly and calls only `useEditorStore.getState().bumpLiveEdit()` (editorStore.ts:300 — bumps `liveEditVersion`, does NOT set `dirty`). The commit lives in `handleMouseUp` at MapViewport.tsx:1362-1400, which restores `target.startX/startY` and then `executeCommand({type:'move-object'...})` (executeCommand is the only caller of `markDirty`, editorStore.ts:396). MapViewport.tsx:1531-1537 `onMouseLeave={() => { ... if (dragTarget.current) dragTarget.current = null; isDragging.current = false; ...}}` runs none of that. There is no window-level mouseup listener in the file (grep for addEventListener finds only keydown at :702 and mousedown/keydown at :1443-1444), so a release outside the container never reaches handleMouseUp either. Consequence chain: `aeonDirty` = `useEditorStore.getState().dirty` (shell/dirty-snapshot.ts:31) feeds `tabHasDirtyDot` (shell/dirty-tabs.ts:41) and the aeon saver's `scope.isDirty` (state/project-runtime.ts:164) — so with no other edit in the session the tab shows no dot, Ctrl+S is a no-op, the close/project-switch guard says nothing is unsaved, and the move is lost. With another edit present it is saved silently and cannot be undone.
findings.fix: Bind the commit to the window (a pointer capture or a `window` mouseup listener, the shape `useWindowStrokeEnd` already uses for the classic composer at components/classic/composer-shared.tsx:145), and make `onMouseLeave` call the same commit path rather than discarding `dragTarget`.

verdict.reasoning: Traced end to end and could not break it. (1) MapViewport.tsx:910-938 sets dragTarget/isDragging on select-mousedown over an object or ring; no setPointerCapture exists anywhere in the file. (2) MapViewport.tsx:1232-1252 mutates the LIVE document — getSectionByIndex (line 840-844) returns useProjectStore's act section by reference, so obj.x/obj.y are the real placement — and calls only bumpLiveEdit (editorStore.ts:300, increments liveEditVersion, never sets dirty). (3) The only commit is handleMouseUp MapViewport.tsx:1362-1400 via executeCommand, which is the only caller of markDirty (editorStore.ts:396; the sole other markDirty is executeAmbientCommand at :474). (4) MapViewport.tsx:1531-1540 onMouseLeave nulls dragTarget and isDragging with no commit, and there is no window mouseup listener — the file's only window.addEventListener calls are keydown at :702 and mousedown/keydown at :1443-1444 for the context menu — so a release outside the container never reaches handleMouseUp, and re-entry does not resume the drag (no onMouseEnter; mousemove with isDragging=false falls to the hover-bar branch). (5) Consequences verified in the stores, not assumed: dirty-snapshot.ts:31 aeonDirty = editorStore.dirty; dirty-tabs.ts:44 returns aeonDirty for a level tab, so no dot; core/editing/save-coordinator.ts:98-105 skips saveActive when scope.isDirty is false and project-runtime.ts:164 defines that scope as tabHasDirtyDot, so Ctrl+S is a real no-op; project-open-guard.ts:49-63 returns {kind:'proceed'} with aeonDirty false, so the project switch/close guard asks nothing and resetProjectRuntime discards the move; and core/project/aeon/save.ts:85-92 serializes section.objects/section.rings verbatim, so with any other edit present the move is written to disk with no undo entry. Concrete trigger: aeon level, select tool, press an object, drag past the viewport edge (toward the inspector/palette panel), release — the object renders at the new spot, dirty stays false, undo has nothing, Ctrl+S no-ops, close prompts nothing. Two nits in the seat's evidence that do not rescue the code: Save All (Ctrl+Shift+S) WOULD persist it, because the aeon saver's top-level isDirty is openEngine()==='aeon' (project-runtime.ts:159) rather than a dirty check, so 'invisible to save' is true only for Ctrl+S; and the fix shape it cites is corroborated — composer-shared.tsx:130-145 documents this identical onMouseLeave-discards-the-stroke bug being fixed for the classic composer with a window mouseup.
verdict.severity_correction: high — the defect is real and silent, but the magnitude is one placement per occurrence and the on-disk project is never corrupted: the lost case discards a single object/ring move (redoable by dragging again), and the saved case writes exactly the position the user intended, merely without an undo entry. Save All also still persists it (project-runtime.ts:159), so it is not fully invisible to the save path. Reserve critical for losses the user cannot reconstruct; this is a broken main-path interaction plus a lying dirty flag.

findings.title: BG-layer tile painting mutates the layout with no command — un-undoable, and Ctrl+Z reverts an unrelated FG edit instead
findings.claim: `paintBgTile` writes straight into the resolved BG nametable and calls `markDirty()` + `bumpLiveEdit()` with no command dispatch, so every BG paint stroke is outside history; the next Ctrl+Z on the act tab pops whatever FG/object command preceded it and silently reverts that instead.
findings.evidence: MapViewport.tsx:744-769: `resolved.layout[tile.tileIndex] = newNt; sectionRenderer.markBgDirty(...); useEditorStore.getState().markDirty(); useEditorStore.getState().bumpLiveEdit();` — no `executeCommand`. It is a first-class drag path (mousedown MapViewport.tsx:948-952 sets `isPaintDragging`, mousemove MapViewport.tsx:1199-1202 re-enters it). editorStore.ts:90-96 admits this by name ("level mutations that DON'T go through a command and so never reach an undo stack ... a direct BG tile write"). A `set-bg` command type exists (core/editing/commands.ts:131-140) but is a whole-plane swap, not a per-tile edit, and nothing on this path builds one. Failure scenario: stamp a chunk (one `set-tiles`/batch on `level:<zone>:<act>`), switch editingLayer to 'bg', paint 30 BG tiles, press Ctrl+Z — the 30 BG tiles stay and the chunk stamp disappears.
findings.fix: Give the BG plane a per-tile command (a `set-bg-tiles` sibling of `set-tiles`, or reuse `set-tiles` with a plane discriminator) and coalesce the drag into one entry on mouseup, the way the classic viewport already does for its stamp gesture (components/classic/ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:896-908).

verdict.reasoning: Could not refute; traced end to end. (1) Reachability: facet-chrome.ts:85 makes `layout` plane-gated so the BG chip renders (LevelWorkspace.tsx:138-141), and facet-tools.ts:20 puts `paint-tile` in the layout facet — so "BG plane + Paint Tile" is a real UI combination. (2) MapViewport.tsx:948-954 returns from the mousedown handler via paintBgTile() before ever reaching the executeCommand({type:'set-tiles'}) at 965; mousemove 1200-1203 does the same for the drag. (3) paintBgTile (744-769) writes resolved.layout[...] = newNt and calls only markBgDirty/markDirty/bumpLiveEdit — no command. (4) resolveActiveBg (61-73) returns the LIVE arrays by reference (entry.layout or act.bgLayout), and core/project/aeon/save.ts:148-154 explicitly persists "BG-layer painting" to data/editor/<zone>_<act>_bg.bin, so the mutation is durable project state. (5) No mouseup coalescing: handleMouseUp (1338-1403) only clears isPaintDragging at 1339; by contrast object/ring drags ARE converted into move-object/move-ring commands at 1374/1389, proving bumpLiveEdit is a transient clock there and the BG case is a permanent gap (editorStore.ts:90-96 names it). (6) Undo scoping confirmed: set-tiles is act-scoped (ZONE_SCOPED_COMMAND_TYPES at editorStore.ts:410-414 lists only set-palette-line/set-tileset-tiles/set-chunk) and executeCommand pushes onto focusedHistory() (editorStore.ts:388-395), the same stack LevelWorkspace.tsx:98-101 pops on Ctrl+Z. (7) set-bg (commands.ts:131-140, history.ts:81-88) is a whole-plane swap of act.bgLayout/bgTiles, never built on this path, and would not even cover the bgLibrary-entry case paintBgTile can hit. Concrete trigger: aeon act tab, Layout facet, stamp a chunk (one act-scoped command), click BG chip, drag-paint N BG tiles, press Ctrl+Z — the BG tiles stay (and save to disk) and the chunk stamp is reverted instead.
verdict.severity_correction: Severity high is correct as stated; explicitly NOT critical — the painted BG data is neither lost nor corrupted (it persists and saves), and the wrongly-undone FG command is recoverable via redo. The defect is a broken main-path feature (undo silently acts on the wrong edit), which matches "high".

findings.title: Aeon composer's tile-space tools and doc-local pixel path mutate the open document with no history entry
findings.claim: `applyTileCell` (tile-stamp, collision paint, palette-apply) and the doc-local branch of `commitWrites` mutate the open ComposerDoc in place and only call `markOpenDirty()` + `bumpDoc()`; neither reaches an undo stack, so Ctrl+Z on the art facet reverts an unrelated `set-tileset-tiles`/`set-chunk` command while the composer edit stays.
findings.evidence: ComposerCanvas.tsx:313-344 — `stampTile(doc, cx, cy, ...)` / `applyPaletteLineToDocCell(doc, ...)` / `paintDocCollision(doc, ...)` all mutate `o.doc` and end at `markOpenDirty(); bumpDoc();` with no `executeCommand`. It is guarded only against live-tile docs (ComposerCanvas.tsx:420-427), so it is fully live for CHUNK documents — the headline chunk-authoring workflow. ComposerCanvas.tsx:255-261 is the same shape for pixels: `adoptPaletteLineForEmptyCells(...); setPixels(doc, atlas, writes); markOpenDirty(); bumpDoc();`. artStore (state/artStore.ts:14-22, 40) holds `open` outside the DocumentHistoryHub entirely — there is no `doc:art:` factory in state/history-factories.ts:51-81. Meanwhile `focusedHistory()` on the art facet resolves to `zoneart:<zone>` (state/editorStore.ts:195, 205-224), a populated BoundEditHistory. Failure scenario: edit a tile's pixels (records `set-tileset-tiles`), switch to the collision tool, paint 10 chunk cells, press Ctrl+Z — the collision paint stays and the pixel edit is reverted. This is the exact class canvas-history.ts's R13 note and canvasStore.ts:263-271 were written to close, still open one surface over.
findings.fix: Either give the composer document its own hub stack (a `doc:art:` factory + a snapshot of `{cells, collisionA, collisionB}` plus the local tile pixels), or convert stamp/collision/palette-apply into commands. At minimum, disable Ctrl+Z while an unsaved composer doc has un-commanded edits rather than letting it hit the zone-art stack.

verdict.reasoning: I traced every link and none breaks. (1) ComposerCanvas.tsx:313-344 `applyTileCell` mutates `o.doc` via stampTile/applyPaletteLineToDocCell/paintDocCollision and ends at markOpenDirty()+bumpDoc() with no executeCommand. (2) Reachable: ArtToolDock.tsx:16-18 exposes tile-stamp/collision/palette-apply; ComposerCanvas.tsx:410-443 builds hostPointer for them; PixelViewport.tsx:214-242 routes pointer down/move/up to it; the only bail is liveTileIndex!==null (line 420), so chunk/new docs are live. (3) No `doc:art:` factory exists — history-factories.ts registers only level:, zoneart:, doc:sprite:, doc:canvas:, and grep for "doc:art" has no hits anywhere. (4) focusedDocId() (editorStore.ts:205-224, ZONE_ART_FACETS at 195) maps the art facet to zoneart:<zone>; for aeon that factory returns aeonLevelHistory() (a BoundEditHistory), which LevelWorkspace.tsx:94-107 pops on Ctrl+Z. Concrete trigger: aeon project, act tab on the art facet, open an existing chunk; pencil a pixel on an atlas-backed cell (commitWrites chunk branch, line 242, records set-tileset-tiles on zoneart:<zone>); switch to the collision tool and paint cells (buffer-only); press Ctrl+Z — the pixel edit reverts, the collision paint stays. docs/ART_SUITE.md:244 explicitly promises tile stamp is one Ctrl+Z step, so this is a gap against stated intent rather than a documented design choice. What the finding overstates: the composer doc is a detached scratch buffer, not project state — docFromChunk (core/art/composer-buffer.ts:49-66) deep-copies cells and does `new Uint16Array(chunk.collisionA/B)`, and nothing reaches project.chunkLibrary until handleSave (art-facet.tsx:103-142) issues set-tileset-tiles + set-chunk as real commands; the buffer is flagged "unsaved" with a Save button (art-facet.tsx:261-281) and both openDocumentGuarded/closeDocumentGuarded (components/art/open-document.ts:13-41) confirm before discarding, so no user work is silently lost. Also the commitWrites doc-local branch is narrower than claimed: on a chunk doc only cells with atlasTile===null fall through to setPixels (lines 213-228) — doc-local writes never overwrite existing project pixels, and the allowCow path is copy-on-write into new local tiles by design. The R13/canvasStore.ts:263-271 analogy does not transfer: there the document already had a doc:canvas: stack that one mutation bypassed; here there is no per-doc stack at all, so this is missing undo coverage on an uncommitted buffer, not a mis-routed edit. The seat's fallback fix (disable Ctrl+Z while a composer doc has un-committed edits) would itself regress the properly-commanded atlas pixel edits made in the same session.
verdict.severity_correction: medium — no silent loss or corruption (the doc is a detached copy, edits are flagged unsaved, and discarding is confirm-guarded) and no wrong output; the harm is that Ctrl+Z on the art facet silently pops an older zone-art command instead of the composer gesture just made, an undo-coverage/consistency defect in a shipped surface, contradicted by ART_SUITE.md:244 but not a broken main-path feature.

findings.title: Aeon map paint-tile / paint-collision drags record one undo entry per cell
findings.claim: The paint-tile and paint-collision drag handlers call `executeCommand` per crossed cell instead of accumulating the gesture and committing once, so one pencil drag becomes tens of undo entries and, at `MAX_HISTORY = 200`, a couple of drags evict the rest of the session's history.
findings.evidence: MapViewport.tsx:1195-1228: inside `if (isPaintDragging.current && (tool === 'paint-tile' || tool === 'paint-collision'))`, the paint-tile branch calls `executeCommand({type:'set-tiles', entries:[{index, oldNt, newNt}]}, level)` for the single hovered tile (MapViewport.tsx:1216-1224), and the collision branch calls `paintCollisionCell(info, ...)` which itself ends in `executeCommand({type:'set-collision-edit'...})` (MapViewport.tsx:829-836). `handleMouseUp` (MapViewport.tsx:1338-1340) only clears `isPaintDragging` — there is no gesture accumulator. core/editing/history.ts:20-26 does no coalescing and history.ts:3/23 caps at 200 with `shift()`. Failure scenario: drag the tile brush across 60 tiles → 60 undo entries; 4 such drags silently drop the oldest 40 commands of the session. Contrast: classic coalesces correctly — ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:896-908 flattens a whole stamp gesture into one `classicSetLayoutCells`, and TileTab.tsx:238-256 states and enforces "ONE GESTURE = ONE classicEditTiles = ONE UNDO ENTRY".
findings.fix: Accumulate the drag in a ref (the `strokeRef` Map shape ChunkTab.tsx:365-402 uses) and emit one `set-tiles` / `set-collision-edit` command with all entries on mouseup, ending on the window so a release outside the viewport still commits.

findings.title: Undoing a sprite frame delete restores the frame but not the animation steps it re-indexed
findings.claim: `deleteFrame` records a `SpriteSnapshot` and then writes both `frames` and `steps`, but `steps` is not a snapshot field — so undo restores the frame while every timeline step that referenced a later frame stays shifted down by one, permanently mis-pointing the animation.
findings.evidence: spriteStore.ts:541-552: `recordEdit(s);` then `const steps = s.steps.filter((st) => st.frameIndex !== removed).map((st) => (st.frameIndex > removed ? { ...st, frameIndex: st.frameIndex - 1 } : st)); set({ frames, steps, currentIndex });`. `snap()` (spriteStore.ts:282-289) and `SpriteSnapshot` (core/editing/sprite-history.ts:7-14) contain frames/currentIndex/selection/paletteMode/zoneLine/standalonePalette — no `steps`. `writeSpriteSnapshot` (spriteStore.ts:405-416) installs only those fields, so `steps` is untouched by undo. The store even documents the split at spriteStore.ts:557-560 ("steps live OUTSIDE the snapshot history") but the delete path violates it by recording a step that half-restores. Failure scenario: a 10-frame sprite with a walk cycle [0,1,2,3]; delete frame 1 (steps become [0,1,2] pointing at old frames 0,2,3); Ctrl+Z restores all 10 frames but the walk cycle now plays frames 0,1,2 — silently the wrong animation, and it will be written to `<name>_anims.asm` on export.
findings.fix: Add `steps` to `SpriteSnapshot`/`snap()`/`cloneSpriteSnapshot` (it is a small array; the cost argument that keeps frames deep-cloned does not apply), or make `deleteFrame` not touch `steps` and re-derive them on read.

findings.title: Saving a NEW chunk appends tiles undoably but adds the chunk un-undoably — one Ctrl+Z strands the chunk pointing past the tileset
findings.claim: The save-chunk path issues `set-tileset-tiles` (an undoable append) and then `useProjectStore.getState().addChunks([saved])`, which is outside history; undoing the tile append leaves a chunk in the library whose nametable references tile indices that no longer exist.
findings.evidence: art-facet.tsx:102-110 executes `set-tileset-tiles` with `at: atlas.length, oldTiles: slice.newTiles.map(() => null)` — undoCommand splices those slots back out (core/editing/history.ts:180-191). art-facet.tsx:126-138 then calls `useProjectStore.getState().addChunks([saved])` + `useEditorStore.getState().markDirty()`; `addChunks` (state/projectStore.ts:83-91) is a plain store write with no command. The design note at core/editing/commands.ts:142-151 declares library adds "additive store state outside undo ... non-destructive" — that reasoning holds only because sections reference entries by id, and it does not cover the tile append the same gesture makes. Failure scenario: draw a new chunk using 12 fresh tiles, Save chunk (tileset grows to N+12, chunk added), press Ctrl+Z once — the 12 tiles are spliced out, the chunk stays in the library with nametable entries N..N+11, and every render/export of it reads past the end of `zone.tileset.tiles`. ArtCanvas's stale-doc heal (art-facet.tsx:172-186) only closes the OPEN document; it does not remove the library entry.
findings.fix: Make the pair atomic — either wrap the tile append and the library add in one batch command (adding an `add-chunk`/`remove-chunk` command type), or perform the `addChunks` first and have the undo of `set-tileset-tiles` refuse when a library chunk still references the appended range.

findings.title: Agent-issued classic art edits record on `zoneart:` while the focused facet still routes Ctrl+Z to the layout stack
findings.claim: `classicSetPalette` / `classicEditTiles` / `classicEditBlock` / `classicEditChunkCells` invoked from the agent record on `zoneart:<zone>` (commitArt), but nothing on that path claims the `art` facet, so if the user is on the layout facet the next Ctrl+Z drives `level:<zone>:<act>` and reverts an unrelated layout step while the agent's art edit stays.
findings.evidence: agent-handler.ts:660/666/719 call the classic commands directly; classicLevelStore.ts:634-642 `commitArt` records on `zoneArtDocIdForCurrentZone()` regardless of focus. The read side is `focusedHistory()` → `focusedDocId()` (state/editorStore.ts:205-237), which keys on `useWorkspaceStore.facetFor(activeTab)` and only maps `art`/`palette` to `zoneart:` (editorStore.ts:195). The facet is claimed only by pointer-down/focus-in on a classic surface (components/classic/classic-surface.ts:118-142) — the agent never touches a surface. components/classic/classic-surface.ts:1-10 documents this exact failure ("a Ctrl+Z after a palette/tile/block/chunk edit drove the LAYOUT stack") as the reason that file exists; the agent door was not closed. Failure scenario: user is on Layout with an unstamped chunk in the layout undo stack, asks the agent to recolour palette line 2, presses Ctrl+Z expecting the recolour back — the layout stamp is reverted instead and the recolour survives.
findings.fix: Have the classic agent edit tools claim the matching facet (call `switchFacet(tabId, 'art')` / `'layout'`) before committing, or route undo by the LAST-EDITED document rather than by focus when the two disagree.

findings.title: Every sprite undo entry deep-clones the whole frame set (50 deep, per open document)
findings.claim: `cloneSpriteSnapshot` copies EVERY frame buffer on record, undo and redo, so a one-pixel stroke on a 100-frame character costs a full copy of all 100 frames, and residency is 50 × (total frame bytes) per open sprite document — the cost canvas-history.ts explicitly budgeted for its own surface but never measured here.
findings.evidence: core/editing/sprite-history.ts:19-28 `frames: s.frames.map(cloneBuf)`, with `SPRITE_MAX_DEPTH = 50` (sprite-history.ts:32) passed to SnapshotHistory (sprite-history.ts:46). `recordEdit` (state/spriteStore.ts:275-278) fires on every stroke via `setBuffer` (spriteStore.ts:476-483, called once per gesture from components/sprite/SpriteCanvasHost.tsx:64). Frames come from `loadSprite` over a full mapping set (state/spriteStore.ts:582), which for an engine character is the whole animation sheet. A 120-frame 48×48 sprite is ~276 KB/snapshot → ~13.8 MB per document at the cap, and each stroke allocates and copies all 276 KB. core/editing/canvas-history.ts:41-47 does this arithmetic for the canvas (~1 MB × 40) and picks its cap from it; sprite-history.ts:30-32 only says "far tighter than the shared default" without the frame-count term.
findings.fix: Snapshot only the frame(s) an edit touches (a per-frame delta, or copy-on-write frame array where unchanged frames are shared by reference — the array is already `.slice()`d, so only `frames[currentIndex]` ever differs), and keep the whole-set clone for the structural ops (add/duplicate/delete frame).

findings.title: applyCommand/undoCommand silently no-op on a missing target, burning an undo slot that reverts nothing
findings.claim: `if (!section) return`, `if (arr)`, and the `if (section.objects[cmd.objectIndex])` guards make a command that cannot be applied succeed silently — it is still pushed onto the undo stack and still clears redo, so the user gets a dead undo step and loses their redo branch for nothing.
findings.evidence: core/editing/history.ts:97-98 (`const section = level.sections[cmd.sectionIndex]; if (!section) return;`) and history.ts:110-111 (`const arr = ...; if (arr) for (...)`) and history.ts:129/247 (`if (section.objects[cmd.objectIndex]) ...`). `EditHistory.execute` (history.ts:20-26) pushes and clears redo unconditionally after `applyCommand` returns. The file's own comment at history.ts:59-61 states the opposite rule for `set-palette-line` — "Throw, don't skip: a silent no-op here corrupts history (the command consumes an undo slot without doing anything)" — so the two halves of the same function disagree. Failure scenario: a `set-collision-edit` issued for a section whose `collisionEdit` plane was never seeded (the agent path at agent-handler.ts:333/405 seeds it; a future caller that forgets would not) applies nothing, occupies an undo slot, and wipes the redo stack.
findings.fix: Apply the `set-palette-line` rule uniformly: throw on a missing section / missing collision plane / out-of-range object index, or return a boolean from `applyCommand` and have `execute` refuse to record a command that applied nothing.

findings.title: core/editing/history.ts — the aeon command engine with 20 hand-rolled inverses — has no unit test
findings.claim: There is no test file for `EditHistory`/`applyCommand`/`undoCommand`; the index-sensitive inverses (`add-object` → `pop`, `add-rings` → `splice(len - n, n)`, `delete-objects` → sort-ascending re-insert, `set-tileset-tiles` → backwards splice of appended slots) are entirely unexercised, and 6 of the 21 command types appear in no test at all.
findings.evidence: `ls src/core/editing/__tests__/` returns bound-edit-history, canvas-history, chunk-invalidation, classic-domain-history, document-history, save-coordinator, selection-to-chunk — no history.test.ts. `grep -rln "new EditHistory"` finds only src/renderer/providers/__tests__/object-inspector-aeon.test.ts, src/core/editing/__tests__/bound-edit-history.test.ts and the production factory. `grep -rn "add-rings|delete-objects|delete-rings|move-objects|set-bg" src --include='*.test.ts'` returns nothing (only `set-sections` appears, once, in state/__tests__/aeon-doc-history.test.ts:94, and only as a payload — its inverse is never asserted). These inverses rely on a LIFO invariant nothing states or checks, and they are the code that decides whether a user's edits come back.
findings.fix: Add a round-trip property test over `AnyCommand`: for a seeded S4Level, apply a random sequence of commands, deep-compare after undoing all of them, then redo all and deep-compare against the post-apply state. That single test covers all 21 types and would catch any future inverse that assumes the wrong index.
